title: Odds form: multiply by a ratio
summary: Prior odds times the likelihood ratio equals posterior odds, on the medical test and on the spam word “free”.

blocks.title: Prior odds

define.meaning: $\frac{P(A)}{1 - P(A)}$: how many times as likely as not. Odds of 1 to 99 are written $\frac{1}{99}$.
What you believe before the evidence. Here, before the test.

blocks.why: Odds make the update a single multiplication, with no division by $P(\text{positive})$.
blocks.prompt: $P(\text{sick}) = \frac{1}{100}$. Write the odds of sick to healthy as a fraction, sick : healthy.

slips.say: That is the probability. Odds divide by the healthy share, $\frac{99}{100}$.
That is healthy to sick. Put sick first.

hints: Odds compare the sick share with the healthy share.

blocks.title: The likelihood ratio

define.meaning: How many times more likely the evidence is if $A$ is true than if it is false.

blocks.why: This one number is all the test adds. It does not depend on how rare the condition is.
blocks.prompt: A test is positive for 90% of sick people and for 5% of healthy people. Find the **likelihood ratio** $\frac{P(\text{positive} \mid \text{sick})}{P(\text{positive} \mid \text{healthy})}$.

slips.say: That is flipped. Sick goes on top.

check.say: It is above 1, so a positive pushes towards sick.

blocks.title: Posterior odds

define.meaning: What you believe after the evidence.

blocks.why: The whole update in one line: new odds = old odds times the ratio.
blocks.prompt: Prior odds of sick are $\frac{1}{99}$ and the likelihood ratio of a positive is 18. Find the **posterior odds**: $\text{posterior odds} = \text{prior odds} \times \text{likelihood ratio}$.

slips.say: That is the ratio alone. Multiply it by the prior odds $\frac{1}{99}$.

blocks.title: From odds to a probability
blocks.why: Odds of $\frac{2}{11}$ are not a probability yet. Check against lesson 1.
blocks.prompt: The posterior odds of sick are $\frac{2}{11}$. Convert to a probability with $P = \frac{\text{odds}}{1 + \text{odds}}$. Give a fraction.

slips.say: That is the odds. Sick is 2 parts out of 13.
That is healthy. Sick is the 2.

hints: Odds 2 to 11 means 2 sick for every 11 healthy.
How many people are in 2 + 11 parts?
blocks.solution: $\frac{2}{13}$ again, the third way to the same answer.

blocks.title: Update on the word free
blocks.why: The same rule works for any evidence. Here it is a spam filter.
blocks.prompt: $P(\text{spam}) = \frac{1}{5}$. The word “free” is in $\frac{3}{5}$ of spam and in $\frac{1}{20}$ of ham. Find the odds of spam after seeing “free”.

slips.say: That is the ratio alone. Prior odds are $\frac{1}{4}$, not 1.
That is the probability from lesson 2. The question asks for odds, which here is $\frac{3/4}{1/4}$.

hints: Prior odds first: spam to ham.

check.say: Odds of 3 are $P = \frac{3}{4}$, the answer from lesson 2.

blocks.solution: Odds 3 to 1 is a probability of $\frac{3}{4}$, matching lesson 2.
